title: Sensex Falls 989 Points as IT Profit-Taking, Oil and a Weak Rupee End Two-Day Rally
excerpt: The Sensex closed at 83,339.26 and the Nifty at 25,607.20 on Friday, November 27, as investors booked profits in IT and banking heavyweights after a two-day rally. Metal stocks, midcaps and smallcaps bucked the fall.
body:
• The Sensex closed 989.33 points lower, down 1.17%, at 83,339.26 on Friday, November 27, and the Nifty fell 277.30 points, or 1.07%, to 25,607.20, snapping a two-day winning streak.
  • Profit-taking in IT heavyweights after a strong run led the fall: the Nifty IT index dropped 1.88% after gaining 3.66% in the previous session, with HCL Technologies down 3.03%, Infosys 2.68% and TCS 2.57%.
  • Rising crude — Brent approached $97 a barrel — a weaker rupee and higher domestic bond yields weighed on sentiment, according to market reports.
  • The fall was narrow: midcap and smallcap indices closed higher and more stocks advanced than declined, so diversified portfolios fell less than the headline indices.

Indian benchmark indices snapped their two-day winning streak on Friday, November 27, with the Sensex plunging 989.33 points, or 1.17 per cent, to close at 83,339.26 and the Nifty declining 277.30 points, or 1.07 per cent, to 25,607.20. The Sensex fell as much as 1,120.26 points intraday, touching 83,208.33, before recovering slightly into the close.

Market reports attributed the fall to profit-taking in heavyweight IT stocks and HDFC Bank, coupled with rising crude oil prices, a weaker rupee and higher domestic bond yields. Brent crude approached $97 per barrel during the session, and the rupee weakened to ₹92.62 against the US dollar in early trade.

IT gives back its gains

Information technology was the day's biggest drag. The Nifty IT index fell 1.88% after gaining 3.66% in the previous session and rising for four consecutive sessions. HCL Technologies declined 3.03% to ₹1,424.10, Infosys slipped 2.68% to ₹1,151.30 and Tata Consultancy Services fell 2.57% to ₹2,572.50. Bajaj Broking's closing report said a tentative recovery in global AI stocks also raised concerns that foreign investment flows could shift to other Asian technology markets.

Financials added to the pressure. The Nifty Financial Services index declined 1.33%, Nifty Bank slipped 0.78% and Nifty PSU Bank fell 0.40%. Shriram Finance was the biggest loser among Nifty 50 stocks, down 3.99% to ₹923.50. Autos and realty also fell after strong previous sessions: the Nifty Auto index declined 1.48%, with Bajaj Auto down 3.36% to ₹10,485, and the Nifty Realty index dropped 1.42% after a 3.27% gain on Thursday. The Nifty FMCG index fell 0.94%.

"IT, Financial Services, Realty and Auto were the major laggards, each declining more than 1%. Metals and Chemicals, meanwhile, led the gains, rising over 1% apiece."

— Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, quoted in BusinessLine

What held up

Metals were the standout gainers, with the Nifty Metal index up 1.38%; JSW Steel gained 1.40% to ₹1,321.20 and Hindalco advanced 0.82% to ₹923. Bharat Electronics was the biggest Nifty 50 gainer, up 1.72% to ₹411.45, while Titan and SBI Life Insurance also advanced. From the Sensex pack, Bharat Electronics, Titan, InterGlobe Aviation, Tata Steel, Power Grid and Trent were the winners, while HCL Technologies, Infosys, TCS, Bajaj Finserv, Tech Mahindra and Axis Bank were among the major laggards.

The broader market told a different story from the headline indices. The Nifty Midcap 100 gained 0.10% to 61,846.30 and the Nifty Smallcap 100 advanced 0.56% to 19,481.30, and market breadth was positive: of 3,748 stocks traded, 2,119 advanced, 1,514 declined and 115 were unchanged. Despite Friday's correction, Bajaj Broking noted the Sensex and Nifty remained higher by approximately 903 points and 258 points respectively over the last three trading sessions.

What investors are watching

Two external threads run through Friday's session: crude prices, with Brent near $97 amid Middle East supply concerns, and US tariff uncertainty. Bajaj Broking reported that the US administration has proposed fresh tariffs on imports from several trading partners including India, with a proposed rate on Indian goods of up to 25% that could be reduced to 17% if a bilateral trade agreement is finalised. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal indicated on Friday that the India-US trade agreement was nearing completion. Further developments on the agreement remain crucial for Indian exporters and overall market sentiment.

nri_angle: The sell-off was concentrated in large-cap IT and financial stocks; broader midcap and smallcap indices rose, so the headline 989-point fall overstates the day for diversified India portfolios held by diaspora investors.
